questions.q: What three proof points does the lesson say AI hiring actually looks for on a resume?
options: Something deployed, something evaluated, and something documented
A long list of model names with no project behind them
A claim that every project is already production-grade with no number to check
Only a list of certifications, since no project detail is needed
questions.explain: The lesson opens by naming deployment, evaluation, and documentation as the three proof points that carry more weight than a list of tool names.

questions.q: What three things does the action + artifact + framework pattern require a resume bullet to include?
options: Your job title, your start date, and your manager's name
A list of every AI model you have ever heard of
What you did, what you produced, and the technique or tool you used
The company's total revenue and headcount
questions.explain: The lesson defines the pattern as action, artifact, and framework -- with the framework being the named technique or tool behind the work.

questions.q: In the lesson's suggested one-page structure, what comes right after the header and optional summary?
options: The three capstone projects, each with proof-backed bullets
A certificate gallery with no further detail
References from previous employers
A full list of every programming language ever studied
questions.explain: The structure places the three capstone projects early, since they carry the strongest, most specific evidence of ability.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against calling notebook-only work "production" on a resume?
options: Because notebooks cannot run Python code at all
Because a resume should be precise about deployment status, and overstating it is a credibility risk
Because notebook-only projects are always lower quality than deployed ones
Because "production" is a reserved keyword in every AI framework
questions.explain: The lesson lists overclaiming "production" status as one of the common mistakes that weakens an AI engineering resume.

questions.q: How should a candidate decide which of their three capstones to lead with for a specific job posting?
options: By always leading with whichever project took the least time to build
By omitting all three and relying on a buzzword list instead
By listing all three in strictly alphabetical order every time
By checking which model provider, framework, and specialty the posting emphasizes, and leading with the closest match
questions.explain: The lesson's tailoring section recommends matching the posting's emphasis (provider, framework, specialty) when choosing which project to lead with.
